Scene: an invented, historically plausible spatial interpretation of the medieval MAIN CITY mosque courtyard in Granada about 1490, during the late Nasrid period, before the Christian conquest of 1492. The lost site's exact plan and facade are not to be claimed as known: design an original restrained Andalusi courtyard based only on generic period architecture, not a replica of an existing building, not today's new Granada mosque, not an Alhambra palace courtyard.
Primary architecture: a rectangular open paved courtyard enclosed by modest single-storey shaded arcades with plainly formed HORSESHOE ARCHES, rendered in softly weathered pale lime plaster and patches of exposed reddish brick. Across the rear, a modest prayer hall's horseshoe-arched frontage under a simple sloping clay-tile roof. Behind one corner rises a SINGLE plain square masonry minaret, modest and simply proportioned with small plain openings, flat restrained roofline, no ornate monumental tower cap. No domes.
Courtyard: a low broad stone ablution basin with a shallow surface of still water at the center, a few orange trees bearing discreet orange fruit planted in the courtyard beside the stone paving. The basin is practical and unadorned, not a monumental ornamental fountain. No copied palace decoration or famous courtyard composition.

Entire scene confined within the historic mosque courtyard; no surrounding present-day blocks. Balanced quiet spatial depth; keep foreground paving, central basin and rear horseshoe arches legible at small image size.
Style/medium: convincing real-camera photograph appearance of a historical scene, natural soft bright late-morning light, gentle real shadows, slightly warm pale plaster, muted earthen brick, clay roofs and subdued green leaves. Tactile ordinary lime plaster, aged brick mortar, stone paving and clean still water. Restrained authentic material wear. Natural photographic exposure and muted color, no HDR, no cinematic saturation, no painterly or CGI finish.
Absolute constraints: NO PEOPLE or human figures anywhere. No identifiable faces or actual person likeness. No modern buildings, no modern Granada mosque, no cathedral, no Christian church, crosses, bells, soldiers, flags, poles, electric lights or modern fixtures. assets.generationPrompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: historical educational illustration for a Granada city introduction.
Create ONE entirely NEW TEXT-ONLY image, native exactly 1536 x 1024 landscape (3:2), opaque RGB PNG, sRGB. No reference/input photographs.
Primary request: a photorealistic, camera-captured-looking imagined reconstruction of Granada's Sacromonte hillside after the prolonged winter rains of 1963. This is a fictional whole-period scene, not a reproduction of any documentary photograph, actual recorded eviction, identifiable location arrangement or real person's likeness.
Scene/backdrop: modest cave homes dug into a weathered sedimentary rock and clay slope, several small irregular WHITEWASHED cave entrance fronts and simple doors in the middle of the view. Wet mud streaks stain the limewashed walls. Show a localized broken, slumped section of rock and earth above and beside one partially collapsed cave front, settled rubble and soggy ground; the collapse has already happened and nothing is falling. The other cave fronts remain standing. Low simple white chimney stacks emerge from the hillside, sparse scrub bushes grow between them. A muddy clay footpath descends along the slope, with shallow puddles and thin mud runoff trails. Misty gray overcast sky, quiet winter atmosphere.
Foreground: one plain worn fabric mattress, one unbranded metal cooking pot, and one simple wooden kitchen chair form a small group of saved household belongings on a safe flat patch beside the muddy path. These items must be distinct and recognizable, period-plausible for a modest Spanish home in 1963, with no writing, decoration depicting art, or brand marks.
People: a short loose line of THREE tiny anonymous fictional ADULTS far away on the descending path, FULLY REAR-FACING, walking safely down the slope away from the cave homes while carrying a plain bundle or a small household belonging. Each distant adult is only about 4-5 percent of the full image height. Ordinary plain early-1960s coats or jackets and trousers; no ethnically stereotyped features, exotic costume, theatrical pose, uniforms or insignia. No faces or readable facial details. They are far from the settled rubble and not in any active danger.
Composition/framing: wide horizontal view from slightly lower ground toward the hillside, from the general lower Albayzin direction; cave fronts occupy the middle distance, damaged rocky clay slope visible above them, small saved household objects in the foreground and tiny rear-facing walkers in the distance. The whole scene fills the frame naturally with believable perspective and human scale. Do not crop around one person or impose a collage. Do not copy a particular photograph's composition.
Style/medium: convincing restrained documentary-photo appearance as if captured with a normal 35mm camera in the early 1960s, muted monochrome with only a faint faded sepia warmth, true natural textures of damp chalky plaster, clay mud, weathered wood, worn cloth and metal. Moderate natural photographic grain, realistic exposure and soft mist. No simulated printed-photo border, scratches or photographic captions.
Lighting/mood: soft flat gray daylight through mist, natural shadows, quiet aftermath. No dramatic spotlight, dramatic backlighting, HDR, glossy CGI, explosion, action-disaster spectacle or cinematic saturation.
Avoid: bodies, casualties, blood, injuries, violence, police, uniforms, military figures, actual-person likeness, identifiable faces, close-up people, children, stereotyped ethnic faces or clothing, modern cars or any vehicles, modern buildings, modern street furniture, electrical wires or technology, signs, lettering, readable words, readable numerals, brands, logos, symbols, watermarks, captions, borders, frames, borrowed artwork, exact documentary photograph composition. No readable text anywhere in the image.
